fields.outcome: A maintainer or CI job can apply an approved invalidation plan so only affected walkthrough module assets are replaced while proven reusable modules remain unchanged.
fields.scope: Consume an ST-07 invalidation plan; block uncertain plans; execute prerequisite journey modules to establish authentication and application state; capture only regenerate-classified DOM or video assets; preserve reusable module files and metadata; assemble and validate the updated walkthrough transactionally through a library API and CLI. Exclude screenshots, presentation styling, remote asset harvesting, publishing, and source-language dependency discovery.
fields.acceptance: Given an existing two-module profile walkthrough and a plan that regenerates update-profile while preserving sign-in, AutoTour executes sign-in as a prerequisite, replaces update-profile output, leaves sign-in assets byte-for-byte unchanged, writes a valid assembled walkthrough, and leaves the prior output intact if regeneration fails. Plans requiring review are rejected before browsing or writing.
fields.changes: Implemented in commit e92c907a91312cffd4885eed4f19bae12fa1f79b: selective capture controls for DOM and video, prerequisite-only module execution, reusable manifest and capture-step merging, strict plan validation, transactional staging and rollback, a public regeneration API, the autotour regenerate CLI command, agent guidance, documentation, and real browser proofs for both output modes.
fields.decisions: Use a sibling staging directory copied from the existing output, generate selected assets there, validate the complete assembled walkthrough, then swap it into place. Execute non-selected earlier modules for state without replacing their artifacts. Infer DOM versus video regeneration from the existing walkthrough output and reject mixed or unsupported output modes.
fields.verification: Test plan and identity validation, review blocking before capture, prerequisite execution, selective asset replacement, byte-for-byte reusable asset preservation, no-op plans, transactional rollback on capture failure, CLI machine-readable output, and real DOM fixture regeneration.
fields.dependencies: Builds on st-07 invalidation plans and the modular DOM/video assets from st-05 and st-06.
fields.risks: Later modules may rely on earlier browser state, so prerequisites must still execute. Filesystem swaps differ across platforms; failed swaps must restore the previous directory. Reusable module metadata must come from the existing walkthrough rather than newly observed prerequisite execution.
fields.evidence: Frozen AgentHouse evaluation for build c5d5b595ceec9fce626681e8f9ab7e23195c627a passed package metadata, the full test suite, and the focused ST-08 regeneration check mapped to every acceptance criterion.
fields.releasePlan: Include selective regeneration in the next private 0.1.x pre-release from protected develop after the frozen AgentHouse evaluation and GitHub CI pass. Validate the packed npm artifact before any registry publication; this work item does not authorize an npm publish.
fields.rollbackPlan: If selective regeneration corrupts or unexpectedly replaces reusable output, revert the ST-08 implementation and maintenance-loop commits and release the prior known-good package state. Existing walkthrough output remains recoverable because regeneration stages and validates the complete result before replacing the prior directory.

criteria.expectation: Regeneration accepts only a complete plan for the same walkthrough and rejects review, unknown, duplicate, or missing module classifications before browsing.
Earlier reusable modules can execute to establish authentication or application state without replacing their artifacts.
Only modules classified regenerate receive newly captured DOM or video assets.
Reusable module assets and manifest entries remain byte-for-byte or structurally unchanged after successful regeneration.
The resulting walkthrough and player assemble regenerated and reusable modules into one schema-valid output.
Capture or assembly failure leaves the existing output directory unchanged and removes temporary staging data.
A public library API and CLI command return deterministic machine-readable regeneration results suitable for CI.
